```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`inkr` is a CSS-like styling engine for terminal interfaces. It parses
stylesheets written in the `.inkr` language, matches them against a logical
tree of elements and computes the style of each element. It is independent of
any terminal UI framework and does not render anything.

```{r}
library(inkr)
```

The package is installed from GitHub with
`remotes::install_github("menshikovs/inkr")`.

## A first stylesheet

A stylesheet is a sequence of variables (`$name: value;`) and rules
(`selector { property: value; }`). Comments use `/* ... */`.

```{r}
text <- "
  $primary: #7c3aed;

  Screen { color: white; background: #181825; }
  Button { background: blue; padding: 1 2; }
  Button.primary { background: $primary; }
"
```

Stylesheets are normally kept in files; `ink_read()` reads a `.inkr` file. The
package ships a few annotated examples:

```{r}
path <- system.file("examples", "basic.inkr", package = "inkr")
basename(path)
```

## Parsing

`ink_parse()` turns text into a syntax tree. Values are still raw text and
variables are not resolved.

```{r}
ast <- ink_parse(text)
ast
```

Malformed input signals a structured `ink_parse_error` with a stable `code`
and a source position:

```{r}
err <- tryCatch(
  ink_parse("Button {\n    color: red\n    padding: 1;\n}"),
  ink_parse_error = identity
)
err$code
conditionMessage(err)
```

## Compilation

`ink_compile()` resolves variables, checks every declaration against a property
registry and turns values into typed objects.

```{r}
sheet <- ink_compile(ast)
sheet
sheet$rules[[3]]$declarations[[1]]$value
```

Compilation does not match selectors or apply the cascade. Invalid values
signal an `ink_compile_error`:

```{r}
err <- tryCatch(
  ink_compile(ink_parse("Button { padding: 1 two; }", source = "app.inkr")),
  ink_compile_error = identity
)
err$code
conditionMessage(err)
```

## Elements

An element describes a component of the running application: a type, an
optional id, classes, active states and a parent. Only parents are stored.

```{r}
screen <- ink_element("Screen", id = "main")
button <- ink_element("Button", id = "save", classes = "primary",
                      states = "focus", parent = screen)
button
```

## Matching

`ink_match()` returns the rules whose selectors apply to an element, with their
specificity.

```{r}
ink_match(sheet, button)
```

## Computed styles

`ink_compute()` applies the cascade and inheritance and returns a typed value
for every registered property.

```{r}
style <- ink_compute(sheet, button)
style
style$values$background
```

`style$provenance` records how each value was obtained, for example whether it
was declared, inherited or the initial value.

```{r}
style$provenance$background$origin
style$provenance$color$origin
```

## Inspecting results

`ink_explain()` answers why a property has its value, listing the winning
declaration and the ones it overrode.

```{r}
ink_explain(sheet, button, "background")
```

The next articles describe selectors and the cascade in more detail
(`vignette("styling-and-cascade", package = "inkr")`) and how a computed style
is adapted to a terminal (`vignette("terminal-styles", package = "inkr")`). The
full language is specified in
[docs/language-spec-v0.1.md](https://github.com/menshikovs/inkr/blob/main/docs/language-spec-v0.1.md).
